provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the nightshades work (2026-10-17): every character from the floras in the nightshades notes (plantgen-claude project-files/nightshades/SOURCES.md), drawn by the rules its taxa hold; drawing values only where no character says them.

taxon.note: WCVP v16 accepted name Capsicum annuum, plant_name_id 2698415 (Library 1.0 list, read 2026-10-17).

growth_form.note: Its habit as the floras describe it, drawn by the forb form.

growth.note: Grown to the age it is drawn at: an annual's one season, a perennial's or shrub's few years.

variants.note: One seed in the open, as the built-in species.

generator.params.note: Drawing values no character gives (nightshades, 2026-10-17): one plant from one seed; stem 10 mm at the foot and two side shoots below the first fork by eye from photographs (iNaturalist 88011298), Bailey (vol. 2 p. 659) giving the varieties as very branchy to few-branched.

allometry.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 2 (1914-17), Capsicum annuum, p. 659 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): the varieties about 2 to 2.5 ft; Wikipedia 'Capsicum annuum': up to 2 m with support. Its reference height is the middle of that range, 0.68 m, at its last keyframe.

traits.life_span.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 2 (1914-17), Capsicum annuum, p. 659 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): grown as an annual in temperate climates.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 2 (1914-17), Capsicum annuum, p. 659 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): the varieties about 2 to 2.5 ft; Wikipedia 'Capsicum annuum': up to 2 m with support.

traits.sympodium.note: Peppers fork past each flower (a dichasium), as the photographs show (iNaturalist 88011298) and as a commonplace of pepper botany; Bailey (vol. 2 p. 659) gives zigzag branches for var. baccatum and flowers solitary at the nodes, not the forking in words.

traits.sympodial_unit_leaves.note: Two leaves, each often with a smaller beside it, on each unit between forks, from photographs (iNaturalist 88011298, 325474352); no source read this session counts them.

traits.leaves_geminate.note: iNaturalist observation 325474352 (CC-licensed photograph, viewed 2026-10-17): a smaller leaf beside the larger at the nodes below the fruit; Bailey (vol. 2 p. 659) gives var. acuminatum dense foliage and var. conoides many leaves. No text read gives it.

traits.flower_posture.note: iNaturalist observation 19920820 (CC-licensed photograph, viewed 2026-10-17): the open flower faces out from its stalk, level or a little down. No text read gives it.

traits.bark_colour.note: iNaturalist observation 88011298 (CC-licensed photograph, viewed 2026-10-17): the stems are green. No text read gives it.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 2 (1914-17), Capsicum annuum, p. 659 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): leaves 2-3 in (var. conoides), often 4 in (var. longum), to 5 in (var. grossum).

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 2 (1914-17), Capsicum annuum, p. 659 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): leaves about 3/4-2 in wide (var. conoides, a fraction unreadable), 2.5 in (var. longum).

traits.flower_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: flower 1-2 cm across; Bailey's corolla widths are unreadable in the scan.

traits.flower_colour.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 2 (1914-17), Capsicum, p. 658 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): flowers white or greenish white, rarely violet. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 2 (1914-17), Capsicum annuum, p. 659 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): fruit 1.75 in or less (var. conoides), 3 in (var. fasciculatum), 3-4 in (bell peppers), to a foot (var. longum).

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Wikipedia, 'Capsicum annuum' (read 2026-10-17): fruit red, yellow, green or black; Flora of British India (p. 239): C. grossum red. The colour is our reading of the word.

traits.fruit_posture.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 2 (1914-17), Capsicum annuum, p. 659 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): fruit erect in var. conoides and fasciculatum, erect or pendent in var. acuminatum; Flora of British India: pedicels nodding in fruit in C. grossum.

traits.flowering_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: flowers June-September.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 2 (1914-17), Capsicum annuum, p. 659 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): the calyx cup-shaped, usually embracing the fruit's base (var. conoides) or saucer-shaped (var. longum); Flora of British India (p. 238): campanulate, much shorter than the fruit.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: fruit from August until frost: like the tomato and eggplant (Bailey vol. 6 p. 3353, vol. 2 p. 1102), a warm-season crop set out after frost; Bailey (vol. 2 p. 659) has the hottest kinds grown only in the South for want of a long enough season.

traits.leaf_colour.note: iNaturalist observation 19920820 (CC-licensed photograph, viewed 2026-10-17): bright, glossy mid green leaves (the leaf pixels of this and iNaturalist 88011298 average [127,154,107] and [141,184,109], lifted by gloss). No text read gives it.
